title: Normalization of an affine base in an algebraically closed point
statement:
Let $Z$ be an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme], $K$ an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and $g:\operatorname{Spec}K	o Z$ any morphism. Then there exist an affine integral scheme $Z^
u$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], an integral morphism $\pi:Z^
u	o Z$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and a field embedding $i:k(Z^
u)\hookrightarrow K$ [def-sc-function-field] such that every local ring of $Z^
u$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $k(Z^
u)$ is algebraically closed, and $g=\pi\circ g^
u$, where $g^
u:\operatorname{Spec}K	o Z^
u$ is the morphism induced by $i$ followed by the generic-point morphism. In particular $g^
u$ is dominant.

source.place: Tags 035H (definition-normalization-X-in-Y), 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization), 035L (lemma-normal-normalization); algebraically closed fraction field as used in Tag 0F08, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold, final proof sentence; explicit exact declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.exists_normalization_of_isAlgClosed, WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/SmoothBaseChange/CurveTestDatum.lean:126-167

proof.text: Write Z as Spec A and let phi:A to K be induced by g; form integral closure B of image A in K.

Set $Z^
u=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Since $B$ is a subring of the field $K$, it is a domain. Applying the existing finite-product integral-closure normality lemma to the one-element product $B^1=K$ gives that every localization $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is an integrally closed domain; hence $Z^
u$ is affine and integral and all its local rings are integrally closed domains. The map from the image of $A$ to $B$ is integral, so the induced morphism $\pi:Z^
u	o Z$ is integral.

For the affine integral scheme $Z^
u$, [def-sc-function-field] identifies $k(Z^
u)$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$. The exact algebraic-closure theorem for the fraction field of an integral closure (the new Mathlib leaf) applies, so $k(Z^
u)$ is algebraically closed. The inclusion $B\hookrightarrow K$ is injective because $B$ is a subring of the field $K$; the universal property of the fraction field therefore gives an injective field homomorphism $i:k(Z^
u)\simeq\operatorname{Frac}(B)\hookrightarrow K$.

Restrict $i$ to $B$ and use contravariance of $\operatorname{Spec}$: the resulting map $g^
u:\operatorname{Spec}K	o\operatorname{Spec}B$ satisfies $g=\pi\circ g^
u$. Its image contains the generic point because $i$ is injective, so $g^
u$ is dominant.

lean.statement:
theorem Etale.exists_normalization_of_isAlgClosed {S' : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S'] {K : Type u}
    [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] (g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S') :
    ∃ (S'' : Scheme.{u}) (_ : IsAffine S'') (_ : IsIntegral S'')
      (_ : ∀ x : S'', IsIntegrallyClosed (S''.presheaf.stalk x))
      (_ : IsAlgClosed S''.functionField) (π : S'' ⟶ S') (_ : IsIntegralHom π)
      (i : S''.functionField ⟶ CommRingCat.of K),
      (Spec.map i ≫ S''.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint S'')) ≫ π = g
lean.note: Exact existing normalization statement. Ring homomorphisms from the function field to K are automatically injective; every stalk of an integral scheme is a domain. The displayed geometric generic-point lift is automatically dominant, since its image is the generic point. These are implicit consequences of the recorded types, not additional hypotheses.
